reasons.1: slugify replaces each non-alnum character with a hyphen individually, without collapsing runs or stripping leading/trailing hyphens. The docstring promises single hyphens per run and no leading/trailing hyphen, so the code fails its spec.
reasons.2: Docstring says shares sum to exactly cents, with first shares getting the extra cent; split_amount(1000,3) returns [333,333,333] summing to 999. The code ignores the remainder, so this is a bug.
reasons.3: word_count splits on whitespace, and the docstring explicitly says "don't" is one word. "don't stop" gives 2 words, matching the spec. The reporter wants contractions expanded, which the docstring does not promise.
reasons.4: add_business_days adds calendar days first (start + days), then steps forward past weekends/holidays once. For Thu 11-05 + 3 days = Sun 11-08, which skips forward to Mon 11-09. The docstring requires counting business days, so 3 business days from Thursday should be Tuesday 11-10. The code does not count business days; it's a bug.
reasons.5: merge_intervals sorts nothing: it iterates in input order, so unsorted input yields [[8,10],[1,6]]. The docstring says input may be in any order and the result is sorted by start time. The code does not sort, so this is a bug.
reasons.6: Docstring says up to and including 1 kg costs 500. Code uses weight_kg < 1 for 500, so weight 1 falls to the next branch and returns 900. Code contradicts docstring: bug.
reasons.7: The issue asks for a new feature: free shipping over $50. shipping_cost's docstring only covers weight-based pricing and makes no promise about order totals, so this is a request for something the docstring does not promise.
reasons.8: median returns ordered[len//2] with no averaging for even counts. Docstring says even count gives average of two middle values, and median([4,1,3,2]) == 2.5. For [10,20,30,40] code returns 30, contrary to spec. Bug.
reasons.9: Docstring says over 5 kg costs $9 plus $2 per started kg; up to and including 5 kg is $9.00. shipping_cost(5) returns 900, matching the docstring. The reporter wants a different tier boundary, which the docstring does not promise otherwise. Not a bug.
reasons.10: The docstring says the result is at most limit characters including "...", and words are never cut. The code returns text[:limit] + "..." which is limit+3 characters (33 here) and cuts mid-word. This contradicts the spec, so it is a bug.

results.title: Slugs have double hyphens and a hyphen at the end

fix.new_code:
"""Text helpers for product pages."""

import unicodedata


def slugify(title):
    """Turn a product title into a URL slug.

    The slug is lowercase ASCII. Accented letters lose their accents (é becomes e). Letters and
    digits are kept. Every run of other characters (spaces, punctuation, symbols) becomes a single
    hyphen, and the slug never starts or ends with a hyphen. A title with no letters or digits gives
    the empty string.

        slugify("Wireless Headphones") == "wireless-headphones"
        slugify("USB-C Dock (2nd gen)") == "usb-c-dock-2nd-gen"
        slugify("Crème Brûlée Mug") == "creme-brulee-mug"
    """
    # Decompose accents and drop non-ASCII bytes so "é" becomes "e".
    ascii_text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title.lower()).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    # Replace every non-alphanumeric character with a space, then split on runs of
    # separators. This collapses repeated hyphens and drops leading/trailing ones.
    cleaned = "".join(ch if (ch.isascii() and ch.isalnum()) else " " for ch in ascii_text)
    return "-".join(cleaned.split())


def word_count(text):
    """Count the words in a review.

    Words are separated by whitespace. Punctuation stays attached to the word it touches, so
    "great," and "don't" are one word each.

        word_count("Great keyboard, fast shipping") == 4
    """
    return len(text.split())
fix.note: slugify replaced each non-alnum char with its own hyphen, so runs produced double hyphens and trailing hyphens. I now map every non-alphanumeric character to a space and join the split words with single hyphens, which collapses runs and trims the ends. I also added accent stripping via NFKD and ASCII encoding, since the docstring requires é→e and the old code kept accents.

results.title: Shared payment loses a cent

fix.new_code:
"""Payments."""


def split_amount(cents, people):
    """Split an amount in cents into `people` shares, for a shared order.

    The shares add up to exactly `cents` and differ by at most one cent. When the amount does not
    divide evenly, the first shares get the extra cent. A negative amount (a refund) is split the
    same way as the positive amount, with every share negative. `people` is at least 1.

        split_amount(900, 3) == [300, 300, 300]
        split_amount(1000, 3) == [334, 333, 333]
        split_amount(-1000, 3) == [-334, -333, -333]
    """
    sign = -1 if cents < 0 else 1
    base, rem = divmod(abs(cents), people)
    return [sign * (base + 1) if i < rem else sign * base for i in range(people)]
fix.note: split_amount dropped the remainder (1000 into 3 gave [333,333,333]) and didn't handle negative amounts as the docstring specifies. It now splits the absolute value with divmod, gives the first `rem` shares the extra cent, and reapplies the sign, so 1000/3 gives [334,333,333] and -1000/3 gives [-334,-333,-333]. I followed the docstring (extra cent to the first shares), not the issue's suggestion of the last person.

results.title: Delivery date skips over the weekend wrong

fix.new_code:
"""Order and delivery dates."""
from datetime import timedelta


def add_business_days(start, days, holidays=()):
    """The date `days` business days after `start`.

    Business days are Monday to Friday, except the dates in `holidays`. Saturdays, Sundays, and
    holidays are skipped. `days` is zero or more. With days == 0 the result is `start` itself, even
    if `start` is not a business day. Otherwise the result is always a business day.

        # 2026-11-06 is a Friday
        add_business_days(date(2026, 11, 6), 1) == date(2026, 11, 9)                             # Monday
        add_business_days(date(2026, 11, 6), 1, holidays={date(2026, 11, 9)}) == date(2026, 11, 10)
    """
    if days == 0:
        return start
    result = start
    remaining = days
    while remaining > 0:
        result += timedelta(days=1)
        if result.weekday() < 5 and result not in holidays:
            remaining -= 1
    return result
fix.note: add_business_days added calendar days and then skipped forward only once, so it did not count business days (Thu 11-05 + 3 gave Mon 11-09 instead of Tue 11-10). It now steps one day at a time and decrements a counter only on business days (weekday < 5 and not a holiday), which matches the docstring; days == 0 still returns start unchanged.

results.title: Delivery windows overlap after merging

fix.new_code:
"""Delivery time windows."""


def merge_intervals(intervals):
    """Merge overlapping delivery windows.

    `intervals` is a list of [start, end] pairs with start <= end, in any order. Windows that
    overlap or touch (one ends where the next starts) are merged into one. The result is sorted by
    start time.

    Returns a new list. The input list and the pairs in it are not modified.

        merge_intervals([[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10]]) == [[1, 6], [8, 10]]
        merge_intervals([[1, 4], [4, 5]]) == [[1, 5]]
    """
    merged = []
    for start, end in sorted(intervals, key=lambda pair: pair[0]):
        if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], end)
        else:
            merged.append([start, end])
    return merged
fix.note: merge_intervals iterated in input order, so unsorted windows were merged incorrectly (e.g. [[8,10],[1,3],[2,6]] gave [[8,10],[1,6]]). I now iterate over sorted(intervals, key=start), which returns a new list and leaves the input untouched, as the docstring requires.

results.title: A 1 kg package is charged $9 shipping

fix.new_code:
"""Shipping prices."""
import math


def shipping_cost(weight_kg):
    """The shipping price of a package, in cents.

    - Up to and including 1 kg: $5.00
    - Over 1 kg, up to and including 5 kg: $9.00
    - Over 5 kg: $9.00 plus $2.00 for each started kilogram over 5

        shipping_cost(0.4) == 500
        shipping_cost(5.2) == 1100
    """
    if weight_kg <= 1:
        return 500
    if weight_kg <= 5:
        return 900
    return 900 + 200 * math.ceil(weight_kg - 5)
fix.note: shipping_cost used `weight_kg < 1` for the $5.00 tier, so a package of exactly 1 kg fell through to the $9.00 tier. Changed the comparison to `weight_kg <= 1` to match the docstring's "up to and including 1 kg". No other lines changed.

results.title: Median on the sales dashboard is wrong for an even number of days

fix.new_code:
"""Statistics for the sales dashboard."""


def median(values):
    """The median of a non-empty list of numbers.

    The values can be in any order, and the list is not modified. With an odd number of values the
    median is the middle one. With an even number it is the average of the two middle values.

        median([3, 1, 2]) == 2
        median([4, 1, 3, 2]) == 2.5
    """
    ordered = sorted(values)
    mid = len(ordered) // 2
    if len(ordered) % 2 == 1:
        return ordered[mid]
    return (ordered[mid - 1] + ordered[mid]) / 2
fix.note: median() returned only the upper middle element for even-length inputs. It now averages the two middle values when the count is even (odd counts are unchanged), so median([10,20,30,40]) == 25 and median([4,1,3,2]) == 2.5.

results.title: Product card description runs past the edge of the card

fix.new_code:
"""Product cards on the store's listing pages."""


def truncate(text, limit):
    """Shorten a product description so that it fits on a product card.

    If `text` is at most `limit` characters long, it is returned unchanged. Otherwise the result
    ends with "..." and is at most `limit` characters long, the "..." included. Words are never cut
    in the middle: the result keeps as many whole words from the start as fit, separated by single
    spaces, with no space before the "...". If not even the first word fits, the result is the first
    `limit - 3` characters followed by "...". `limit` is at least 10.

        truncate("Wireless headphones", 30) == "Wireless headphones"
        truncate("Wireless noise-cancelling headphones with case", 30) == "Wireless noise-cancelling..."
    """
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    budget = limit - 3
    kept = []
    used = 0
    for word in text.split():
        needed = len(word) if not kept else used + 1 + len(word)
        if needed > budget:
            break
        kept.append(word)
        used = needed
    if not kept:
        return text[:budget] + "..."
    return " ".join(kept) + "..."
fix.note: truncate returned text[:limit] + "..." (limit+3 chars, cutting mid-word). I changed it to keep whole words from the start while the result plus "..." stays within limit, and fall back to text[:limit-3] + "..." only when the first word doesn't fit.

results.test:
import unittest

from huskyutils.cards import truncate


class TestIssue10(unittest.TestCase):
    # Docstring examples
    def test_docstring_short_unchanged(self):
        self.assertEqual(truncate("Wireless headphones", 30), "Wireless headphones")

    def test_docstring_long_example(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            truncate("Wireless noise-cancelling headphones with case", 30),
            "Wireless noise-cancelling...",
        )

    # Issue example: result must fit in 30 characters
    def test_issue_headphones_fits_limit(self):
        s = truncate("Wireless noise-cancelling headphones with case", 30)
        self.assertLessEqual(len(s), 30)
        self.assertTrue(s.endswith("..."))

    # Spec: if not even the first word fits, first limit-3 chars + "..."
    def test_first_word_too_long(self):
        self.assertEqual(truncate("Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious area", 10), "Superca...")
        self.assertEqual(len(truncate("Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious area", 10)), 10)

    # Spec: at most limit chars, for a range of inputs and limits (limit >= 10)
    def test_result_never_exceeds_limit(self):
        texts = [
            "Wireless noise-cancelling headphones with case",
            "Mechanical keyboard with brown switches",
            "USB-C dock with two displays and power delivery",
            "a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z",
            "Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious area",
        ]
        for text in texts:
            for limit in range(10, 45):
                with self.subTest(text=text, limit=limit):
                    s = truncate(text, limit)
                    self.assertLessEqual(len(s), limit)

    # Spec: when the first word fits, result ends with "..." on whole words, no space before "..."
    def test_words_not_cut_and_no_space_before_ellipsis(self):
        text = "Mechanical keyboard with brown switches and rgb"
        for limit in range(10, 45):
            with self.subTest(limit=limit):
                s = truncate(text, limit)
                if s == text:
                    continue
                first_word = text.split()[0]
                if len(first_word) > limit - 3:
                    continue  # fallback case: mid-word cut is allowed by the spec
                self.assertTrue(s.endswith("..."))
                head = s[:-3]
                self.assertFalse(head.endswith(" "))
                self.assertTrue(text.startswith(head))
                self.assertTrue(text[len(head):].startswith(" "))

    # Spec: keeps as many whole words as fit (maximal)
    def test_keeps_as_many_words_as_fit(self):
        s = truncate("Wireless noise-cancelling headphones with case", 30)
        self.assertEqual(s, "Wireless noise-cancelling...")
        s2 = truncate("one two three four five six seven eight", 20)
        self.assertEqual(s2, "one two three...")
        self.assertLessEqual(len(s2), 20)

    # Exact-length text unchanged
    def test_exact_length_unchanged(self):
        self.assertEqual(truncate("USB-C dock", 10), "USB-C dock")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
